scopeNote: Methodology and privacy references used to design the MC-10 customer-discovery instruments, plus explicit assumptions. No customer, interview or market-response data is stored here; MC-09 conducted no discovery.

sources.title: pricesensitivitymeter: Consumer Price Preferences and Price Sensitivity Analysis (R package reference manual)
sources.publisher: CRAN, The R Foundation for Statistical Computing
sources.limitations: Implementation documentation that restates the Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity Meter logic and cites the 1976 ESOMAR paper; it is not the original paper and was read as a method description, not as empirical evidence. The original proceedings document was not accessed.

sources.title: Gabor-Granger method (encyclopedia entry)
sources.limitations: Tertiary, openly editable description used only to confirm the name and the buy-response-at-price-points procedure. The original Gabor and Granger article in the Journal of Advertising Research was not accessed; bibliographies disagree between 1964 and 1966 and between volume 4(4) and 6(4). No numeric claim is derived from this source.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation), consolidated text
sources.limitations: Primary law; national implementation (Spanish LOPDGDD, Portuguese law 58/2019) can add requirements and was not examined in MC-09.

sources.title: Guidelines 05/2020 on consent under Regulation 2016/679
sources.limitations: URL reachability and title verified on 2026-10-31; the full text was not quoted, so the consent-design requirements recorded in CLM-MC10-003 are the well-established guideline principles and must be re-checked against the current version before fielding.

sources.title: ICC/ESOMAR International Code on Market, Opinion and Social Research and Data Analytics
sources.limitations: URL reachability and title verified on 2026-10-31; individual clause numbers were not transcribed, so obligations are recorded as principles, not quotations.

claims.claimText: The Price Sensitivity Meter obtains four price judgements per respondent (too cheap, bargain, expensive, too expensive) and derives an acceptable price range from the intersections of the cumulative distributions.
claims.observedValue: 4 price questions; range derived from curve intersections
claims.limitations: Method description only. It says nothing about marine customers, MAREA, or any real price; it justifies instrument design, not a price.

claims.claimText: The Gabor-Granger procedure presents a fixed ladder of price points to each respondent and records buy-response intent at each point, producing a stated-intent demand curve rather than an observed sales curve.
claims.observedValue: fixed price ladder; buy-response intent per point
claims.limitations: Tertiary source; original article not accessed. Stated intent overstates real purchase and the method cannot be used alone to approve a price.

claims.claimText: Consent under the GDPR must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous, must be withdrawable, and requires a recorded affirmative action; silence or pre-ticked boxes are not valid consent.
claims.observedValue: Article 6(1)(a) and Article 7 conditions; EDPB consent guidelines
claims.limitations: Applies to all interview consent and audio recording; national Spanish and Portuguese implementations may add requirements not examined here.

claims.claimText: Research participation must be voluntary and based on adequate information, must not be misrepresented as a sales or promotional activity, and respondent data must be protected and used only for the declared research purpose.
claims.limitations: Recorded as principles because individual clauses were not transcribed; re-check the current code text before the moderator guide is finalised.

claims.claimText: None of the MC-10 willingness-to-pay questions has been asked yet; every price, subscription and bundle WTP value in the programme remains NOT_MEASURED and no customer response data exists.
claims.limitations: Recorded as UNKNOWN per contract rule 3: the missing evidence is real interviews and a funded pricing study. This record must be replaced only when actual field data exists, never by an estimate.

claims.claimText: A purposive quota sample of 5-10 interviews per segment cannot support statistical inference, margin-of-error estimates or population representation, and saturation in a narrow segment is not a prevalence measure.
claims.limitations: Methodological constraint stated as a negative, recorded because no source was accessed to quantify it in MC-09. It is a design rule for the MC-10 analysis plan, not a measured fact.

claims.claimText: Assumption A1: the problem is assumed to differ by role (owner, installer, retailer, operator) but the assumption has not been tested, so MC-10 must interview each role separately before any single segment message is written.
claims.limitations: Explicitly a hypothesis, never a measurement. Tested by EXP-MC10-01, EXP-MC10-02 and EXP-MC10-08.

claims.claimText: Assumption A2: installers are assumed to be the practical gatekeepers for refit-led adoption, so installer objections are assumed to bind before owner enthusiasm converts into an installation.
claims.limitations: Explicitly a hypothesis, never a measurement. Tested by EXP-MC10-02.

claims.claimText: Assumption A3: marina-based owners and marina operators are assumed to share the unattended-vessel problem while wanting different evidence; the shared-problem assumption is untested.
claims.limitations: Explicitly a hypothesis, never a measurement. Tested by EXP-MC10-09.

claims.claimText: Assumption A4: subscription resistance is assumed to be specific to local-only functions rather than to recurring charges in general, so the instrument separates local functions from continuous services instead of asking a single acceptance question.
claims.limitations: Explicitly a hypothesis, never a measurement. Tested by EXP-MC10-03.
